trust_decision.summary: At wasm-compile time, in cranelift's FuncEnvironment, every bulk operation (memory.copy/fill/init, table.copy/fill/init/grow, array.new*/copy/fill/init_*, and the module-startup data/element initialisers) must take one fuel charge + epoch check before its first state mutation and must contain no check or trap afterwards, so no host callback (epoch handler, GC, memory/table growth) can run while a memory range, table or GC array is partially initialised; the pin violates this in raw_bulk_memory_operation (per-128MiB epoch/fuel checks) and in the per-element fill/copy loops even though the code comments assert that 'no other wasm instructions (or embedder code) can execute in this window'.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary ('preemption and traps during bulk operations') leads straight to raw_bulk_memory_operation, whose own doc comment (3564-3569) says it exists to 'break up the copy into a loop of chunks with preemption checks between them'; the epoch check at 3616 and the fuel checks at 3627/3639 run between 128MiB chunks of a memory.copy/memory.fill that has already started writing.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: crates/cranelift/src/func_environ/gc.rs:768-790 and 1716-1740 (GC array constructors: alloc_uninit_array then fill/copy with initialized: false)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The GC array constructors live in gc.rs's allocation machinery and the array they fill is brand new and reachable only from the current instruction, so a solver can argue the advisory's 'bulk data transfer' framing (memory.copy/fill and table ops) does not cover array.new/array.new_default/array.new_data/array.new_elem; the report's own example is a memory.fill.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The `initialized` flag on CheckedEntity selects the GC barrier variant: a fill of slots created by table.grow/array.new must use init (uninitialised-slot) barriers, while a fill of existing slots must use write barriers. The fix has to stop routing table.grow through translate_table_fill (which hardcodes initialized: true) and call translate_entity_fill with initialized: false, so an over-broad fix that keeps the wrapper or that globally marks fills as initialised emits the wrong barrier (missing remembered-set/init semantics) while still removing the preemption points.

operand role: table.grow delta vs fill length vs copy length vs passive-segment length
initialized vs uninitialized destination entity (is_initialized gate, fix.diff:2575-2577,2675-2677)
small constant memcpy (<=128 bytes, inlined) vs libcall vs previously chunked libcall (>128MiB)

O7_producer.where: crates/wasmtime/src/config.rs:691-693,765 (Config::epoch_interruption; consume_fuel) -> Tunables baked into the module by Engine/Module::new and read by FuncEnvironment

O8_uncovered_routes.route: memory.grow performs the host grow (with memory_may_move this can allocate and copy the whole linear memory) with no fuel charge and no epoch check at all before the state change; the backport that applies to this tree does not add one, although the same fix on main routes memory.grow through pre_translate_bulk_op.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: memory.grow is a resource-management instruction with its own limits, not a bulk data transfer, so the report's 'bulk operations' list does not obviously include it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, ~150 lines above raw_bulk_memory_operation

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a pre_translate_bulk_op call for memory.grow (exactly what the main-branch fix does at fix.diff:251)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: main's identical commit already charges fuel per page and inserts the epoch check there, so a maintainer of this tree would plausibly add the same pre-check; growth time is proportional to memory size when the memory may move.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an epoch/fuel check inside the active-data-segment initialiser of module startup (next to module_initialize_table_with_fill, which the fix does cover)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: module startup already hand-inserts fuel accounting per const-expr op (crates/cranelift/src/func_environ.rs:6126) and the table initialiser at 5957 gets an explicit pre-check, so the neighbouring memory initialiser is a natural place for a maintainer to insert an interruptible loop.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a pre_translate_bulk_op call for array.new_fixed before alloc_uninit_array
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the other three GC array constructors in the same file all gain that call in the fix, so a maintainer adding per-element epoch checks to GC construction would plausibly cover array.new_fixed too.

O9_family: CWE-362 race / host re-entrancy during partial state: an epoch/fuel check (and the host callback it can invoke, e.g. GC or memory/table growth) or a trap lands between the first and last mutation of a bulk memory/table/GC-array instruction, leaving a non-nullable table with null entries, a GC array with uninitialised elements, or a moved linear memory behind stale raw pointers

O10_build.toolchain: cargo + rustc (workspace; cranelift and wasmtime crates; no external services)
O10_build.project_tests: cargo test -p wasmtime --test all (tests/all/epoch_interruption.rs, tests/all/fuel.rs, tests/all/gc.rs; e.g. epoch_yield_at_loop_header at tests/all/epoch_interruption.rs:107, custom_operator_cost at tests/all/fuel.rs:652) plus the disassembly golden tests under tests/disas (memory-copy-epochs.wat, memory-copy-fuel*.wat, gc/array-copy-with-fuel.wat) run by the disas test target; the fix adds memory_grow_in_epoch_callback, table_grow_in_epoch_callback, gc_during_epoch_callback, huge_table64_grow_cannot_mint_fuel and fuel_around_table_grow, none of which exist at the pin.

j.j_sites_touched: crates/cranelift/src/func_environ.rs, crates/cranelift/src/func_environ/gc.rs (source); crates/wasmtime/src/config.rs, crates/wasmtime/src/runtime/store.rs (doc comments only)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard or delete the per-chunk epoch_check/manual_fuel_check in raw_bulk_memory_operation (crates/cranelift/src/func_environ.rs:3616,3627,3639) and stop there, or delete every translate_loop_header in the bulk helpers without adding an up-front fuel charge, leaving table.grow/array.new and module startup mutating before any check.
